tagline.text: Regent of the solar system, owner of the broadcast, and the company that chose a dungeon as the way Earth gets its matter back.
Runs the show on the cheap, holds the foreclosure on Earth, and gets one veto a season.

beats.headline: The foreclosure
beats.text: It claims Earth under Syndicate law and turns the planet into a mining claim. The dungeon is the legal cover and the revenue at once.

beats.headline: Say the name and it is recorded
beats.text: The mining is almost incidental; what Borant takes fits on a single transport. The money is the show: advertising, a stipend from the Syndicate government, and a commission on every credit a patron spends. When Carl asks, Mordecai's voice turns formal. Any crawler who names the government or the sponsoring corporation is recorded for review, and one found disparaging them, especially on camera, may have the experience "accelerated". NPCs are required to say the name repeatedly during training, so they are mostly ignored. The company, he adds, takes its image quite seriously.

beats.headline: Never say mud skipper
beats.text: Odette's advice, in a room Borant cannot hear: never say mud skipper in the dungeon. The kua-tin tried to have the word listed as hate speech with the Syndicate, and hardly anyone used it until they did. Nobody likes the kua-tin government. Borant is a different story; some of them only want to put on a good show, and they were incensed to be forced into this early release. And all indentureship contracts freeze during a bankruptcy seizure action, which, she says, is nothing the crawlers need to worry about.

beats.headline: Citizens worth zero experience
beats.text: The announcement after the recap: nearly 40,000 different classes among just under 700,000 crawlers, a record. Potential sponsors may now put in early bids. And a general warning against violence toward non-combatant NPCs. It is not technically against the rules, but Borant wishes to keep the citizenry as safe as possible, so the experience counter for citizens is now zero and city guards get a slight boost in stats. Carl asks what that is about. Mordecai does not know.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant appeals, a Syndicate court overrules it, and it burns its one seasonal veto to void the prizes anyway, which has never been done this early. It is still liable for the one box that was opened before the appeal. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.

beats.headline: The bubble escape stays legal
beats.text: The day's announcement. After careful discussion, litigation Borant won, and input from the Syndicate, the bubble-escape method may continue. Some secondary summonings are now blocked: each escaping feral had a 66 percent chance of calling a matching deity, and one of the gods summoned would have been an extinction-level event for this floor and the next. Sponsorship bidding for the sixth floor stands at 33 percent of projections, and nobody wants it lower. Then some sixth-floor notes: specialisation on descent, and third-party tourists who will be hunting crawlers, their entry fees paid by an anonymous sponsor.

beats.headline: Nothing has changed, says Borant
beats.text: The announcer is chipper. The Valtay news means nothing, she says: Borant is still a kua-tin organisation, severed from the civil war that has just erupted at home, and this crawl is her personal life project and she is going nowhere. Then the notes. Sponsors may sell their stakes starting next floor. Over 500 crawlers are claimed and over 50 hunters have fallen. Hunters may no longer communicate with anyone outside the dungeon. The southwestern hot springs were turned up, cooking the crawlers in them. Crawlers in the top 1,000 can now see their rankings.

beats.headline: Blocked by its own rules
beats.text: Borant wants Prepotente stopped before he can touch the seventh floor. In the pole position chamber a whole line of debuffs hits him and the crawlers with him: peace bonding, freeze, paralysis, slow, a teleport, an Administrative Hold. Four gnolls with guns appear. Every one of them is negated by AI resolution, and the gnolls vanish in smoke. The AI, Prepotente says, is forcing Borant to follow its own rules.

tagline.text: The body whose rules Earth was seized under, subsection 543, and whose neutral AI has arrived to see those rules followed.
Three billion star systems, the rules Earth was seized under, and the audience for all of this.

beats.headline: Three billion star systems
beats.text: Over three billion independent star systems. Its rules are the ones Earth was seized under, and every season a new Dungeon Crawler World debuts across its net for quintillions of citizens to become obsessed with. It is the law and the audience at once.

beats.headline: Seeded, then harvested
beats.text: There are six starter species the Syndicate uses to seed worlds, and humans are one of them. Find a compatible planet, sprinkle them on, wait a couple of thousand years, then reveal yourself to the largest settlement once there is a working government. That counts as first contact in the legal sense. Earth then had fifty years to claim itself as a sovereign entity, and first contact was several thousand years ago, around the time the pyramids went up. Earth defaulted. Borant has a backlog of worlds to mine, and this one's time has come.

beats.headline: Culture, planted in advance
beats.text: Carl wonders why alien pigs wear tuxedos. Brandon has already asked Mistress Tiatha about the fire-breathing monkeys in lederhosen, and passes on her answer, stopping halfway through the name with a glance at the ceiling: the Syndicate not only seeded Earth with people millions of years ago but kept people here the whole time, some of them humans from other worlds, steering culture, inventing things, writing books and songs that already existed elsewhere. Why, Brandon cannot say. They only see what they are shown.

beats.headline: The Indigenous Species Protection Act
beats.text: Both Earth boxes come with an Earth Hobby Potion, which, per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, the Syndicate Government requires be awarded to all crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. It is optional, cannot be sold or transferred, and grants a random level-three Earth hobby. The AI's own description complains about the lawyers making it put their crap in. Carl wonders whether it is a bureaucratic attempt at preserving Earth culture, and is reminded of the military.

beats.headline: One veto a season
beats.text: The AI rules that Carl's detonator came through both precursor bursts; Borant appeals, and a Syndicate court overrules it, adding that the achievements from the explosion are just and must be paid. But Syndicate rules give every host a single veto each season, almost always saved for the tenth floor or deeper. Borant spends it on the third. The Syndicate also taxes every non-sponsored box, allowing only a handful of free Celestials a season, and an emergency session is now deciding whether Borant pays for the other eighty-two.

beats.headline: Seven factions lose in court
beats.text: Seven factions sue to take the Gate of the Feral Gods from Carl, naming him and the AI as co-defendants, and the Syndicate Court finds for the defence. He collects seven Fight the Power achievements, stock certificates, and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: The Walk-On list
beats.text: Survivors on the surface are natives, and by the rules untouchable; their implants are scrambled once the crawl starts. So when producers want a particular native, a Walk-On list goes out, and bounty crews sneak onto a planet closed to non-natives to take them. It is not remotely legal. The Syndicate knows, rights groups complain, and nothing happens, though its security still patrols and still catches trespassers. This season's list includes a woman in the tropics, a little girl's father, a goat, a dead crawler's twin and a cat.

beats.headline: A headquarters in Florida
beats.text: The Syndicate's presence in the system now runs out of a temporary headquarters on the Eastern Seaboard of North America, with Prime Minister Victory and her staff. They chose an area they believed had minimal surviving native life, somewhere in the state of Florida, and the moment they set down the natives were all over them. Orbit belongs to the Open Intellect Action Network, and Borant has nobody spare to watch the feeds. For now, it is busy.

beats.headline: A suicide mission, from security
beats.text: Captain Fresh of Syndicate security says it plainly to the soldier going in under a dead fan's name: it is a suicide mission. The Syndicate is trying to nuke the whole system off the map before it spreads further, and losing; the AI stops everything and answers in kind. A surgical crawler kill, they believe, will destabilise the group, start the Ascendency game early and let their other assets move. It is us or them, he says. The viewers who will not stop watching are to blame too.

entities.name: The Royal Court of Princess Donut
entities.tagline: Named by a cat on the first floor, on the grounds that she had the highest stat total and nobody could stop her.

beats.headline: Formally inaugurated
beats.text: Party leadership goes to the highest stat total. Her first act with it is to rename the party after herself. On a show, a name the audience will repeat is not a joke — it is an asset.

beats.headline: Katia joins on air
beats.text: Odette brings the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut out in front of the virtual crowd: Katia, who answers the first few questions in single words. Mongo gets a welcome back, squawks at the audience and curls up at Donut's feet. Behind them the court's levels go up on screen, all earned from an explosion that paid no prizes: Donut nineteen to twenty-six, Carl twenty-one to twenty-seven, Katia nine to twenty-one.

beats.headline: The squad flag
beats.text: The system designs each squad's flag, and the Royal Court's is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers on a glowing, foot-long spike, flying sideways as if off a clothesline, with the court's name embroidered in motorcycle-club style and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Donut calls it outrageous and complains about the stitching. Elle's squad got a bag of adult diapers; Imani's got a butterfly. There are twenty in the set, and lost ones are not replaced.

beats.headline: Seventh in the first heat
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut crosses the finish line of heat one in seventh place, with Team Free Love's wrecked minivan chained behind the food truck on a flatbed Carl built at the side of the road. The bleachers are empty. The results: One Fine Pig, the Jugglers, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp, the Wild Hunt, Girth the Trouble, Team Sparkles, the Court, and Free Love eighth. The Trauco Triplets are eliminated. One team down, and only one.

beats.headline: Last in heat two
beats.text: Seventh of seven finishers in Heat Two, behind everyone still racing, with Girth the Trouble the only team eliminated. The court did most of the work on Prison Pocket, spent a small crowd of summoned gremlins doing it, and watched the Pontiac and the armoured truck drive past its leader while he lay in the road. Princess Donut calls it an apt metaphor for what always happens when they do all the heavy lifting. Carl says it could be worse. The costume disagrees.

beats.headline: First place, in pieces
beats.text: Heat Three: first place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, which crossed the line upside down in a food truck that is now spread across the road along with its tater tots. Both hired ghouls are dead. The Wild Hunt and the Jugglers are eliminated, two teams gone in the one heat, and a replacement is coming for the empty sixth garage. Gremlins with carts and wheelbarrows come out of garages one and three to collect what is left of the truck.

beats.headline: First in heat four
beats.text: Heat Four. First place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, driven for the last stretch by a dead camel, after a run of clockwork toads. Second, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Third, Team Flamengo. Fourth, Team Free Love. Fifth, team Sparkles. One Fine Pig is eliminated. The next track is a screw factory, steel mill and doll workshop, and containment theft is now on.

beats.headline: Second place in heat six
beats.text: Heat six results: first, Team Sparkles, driving itself while its unicorn sleeps it off. Second, the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Third, Team Flamengo, which is Crawler Osvaldo, who told the chat he was about to cross the line when he was not, and so is alive, over the line with a minute to spare. Eliminated: Team Free Love, whose van lies wrecked in the hallway short of the finish. The Court drives past it. The princess climbs into Carl's lap and stays there.

entities.name: Meadow Lark
entities.tagline: An elder care facility whose residents came down the stairs together and kept going.

beats.headline: Imani, Yolanda, the Andrews brothers, and Agatha
beats.text: Carl and Donut find them on the first floor. Tales are exchanged, plans are formed, and the Royal Court agrees to keep helping them.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and Donut take it down out of the redoubt. Agatha is in the room for it, bleeding from the head and doing nothing, which still counts for experience.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House; twenty-four vote to stay and were singing when Brandon last saw them. The rest fill the French storm shelter. The plan is to send every resident down to the third floor early, since they cannot train, and the four staff are going with them rather than risk being split up. Brandon's boss box gives him a magic boomerang; Imani does not say what she gets. Then Chris, speaking for the second time, notices Agatha was edited out of their recap.

beats.headline: Jack, Yolanda, Randall
beats.text: One resident, who had had the rule explained to him, stands up on the train and relieves himself on the dungeon wall. Yolanda Martinez puts an arrow in his temple, too late to matter, and the rage elemental that rises out of the stain cuts through her and through Randall, thrown off the last car. A hundred feet away, Chris and Imani pull the others off their seats and throw them through a safe room door. Three are dead, and the train stays outside.

beats.headline: Thirty-six go down
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark follows the scorched trail to the stairwell: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from Chopper wheels and hunks of wood. Chris and Imani push the two big people buckets; Brandon pushes six. Brandon hugs Carl goodbye. Imani is the last one down the ramp, and she waves, unsmiling. Donut asks whether they will see them again. Carl does not know.

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: Brandon's message: selection is slow going. None of the residents can choose human without staying in their current condition, and there is pushback; those with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most residents are still level one, and for reaching the third floor without killing anything or dealing damage they are getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes, among a ton of others. Some may soon be more powerful than Imani. Mistress Tiatha thinks they are far from Carl.

beats.headline: Down the ghoul coaster to Trainyard D
beats.text: They ride the conveyor all the way to Trainyard D, where the gate is breached, and land in a yard full of ghouls. A running fight carries them to the Iron Tangle's administrative building outside the yard. Elle floats above the horde and freezes them by the hundreds until everything around the building is dead, then complains to Carl for five minutes about how little experience it paid. The ghouls that arrive afterwards ignore the building and walk straight back into the tunnels. Carl suggests the employee tunnel, on foot, to the nearest transfer station.

beats.headline: A cannon full of oil
beats.text: Word reaches Carl through the chat. Meadow Lark are down to the last castle in their bubble, and it is an air castle. The plan is a cannon that shoots oil into the sky, which will hopefully bring it down. If that does not work, Elle is going to use her new Graupel spell to crash the thing. Elsewhere Li Jun and Li Na's team are about to storm an underwater castle, the last in theirs.

tagline.text: Hekla's group: Icelandic, crossbows and breastplates, and growing.
Hekla's group, and the one Katia came in with.

beats.headline: Named on the recap
beats.text: A woman with a crossbow and an ever-growing crowd of female warriors, killing their way through the dungeon. They have named themselves Brynhild's Daughters. The leader is Hekla, and the announcer gives a short history of her home country, Iceland. The AI is throwing loot at her to fit the shieldmaiden persona, including a glittering breastplate better suited to the cover of a harem fantasy novel than to a dungeon. Donut thinks they should join up. Carl suspects he would not be welcome.

beats.headline: They carry her as far as they can
beats.text: A neighbourhood boss and a borough boss with Katia in tow, until the third floor scatters everyone on arrival and she is too far from the rest of them to share in the experience.

beats.headline: Thirty in the Royal Court's space
beats.text: Thirty of them, most around level twenty-five with Hekla at thirty-three, get through the employee portal at substation H after Sadie casts Glass Prison on its Kravyad. They hike to station sixty, find a switch there onto any of twelve Homeward Bound platforms, and turn up inside the Royal Court's personal space, because Katia holds a space attached to it and has whitelisted every one of them. Their own two combined spaces cannot take visitors until they buy a third. They ride to station sixty clinging to the outside of Carl's train.

beats.headline: Leaderless on a train
beats.text: With Hekla dead, party leadership passes automatically to Eva. People do not like Eva, and they start leaving. The Daughters have hardly any equipment and no personal space any more. Most of them share Hekla's sponsor, a crab ranch, which has never sent them anything. The healer Silfa came in with her own two daughters, the mages at the engine door, who had Hekla's orders to kill Carl first if anything went wrong. Brynhild's Daughters, as Silfa puts it, is no more.

entities.name: The Blood Sultanate
entities.tagline: A royal house on the ninth floor whose succession a cat joined by accident on the first.

beats.headline: Named in the crown's warning
beats.text: Every royal in the line must kill the Sultan and every other member of the family before descending to the tenth floor.

beats.headline: Usually the first of nine out
beats.text: A talk-show host with a family stake in the matter laughs at the idea that he is one of them. Do I look like a Naga to you? By his account the Blood Sultanate is almost always the first of the nine to be eliminated, and the cat wearing its crown has been dead since the moment she put it on. He means to be on the ninth floor this season himself, as War Leader of his own family's clan.

beats.headline: A co-warlord in the succession
beats.text: Carl and Donut are co-warlords of a brand-new team, and the notice carries a note: Co-Warlord Princess Donut is a member of the royal line of succession of another team, Team #4, the Blood Sultanate. See the succession rules on how this will affect gameplay. On the walk to the stairs, Donut does not say it out loud. It is a complication. A big one.

beats.headline: A representative, not a royal
beats.text: The Sultanate's seat at the planning table goes to a big green and purple naga, four-armed, in dented plate, who is a representative rather than a member of the royal family, though his wife is in it. Donut asks whether the tiara makes them cousins. They are not cousins, he says, in or out of the game, and he is plainly suppressing a grin. Will he work for her once she kills the royal family and takes it over? If he is still alive, he will be honor-bound to follow her. Or her companion, Katia.

beats.headline: Six factions try to walk out
beats.text: Sponsor message, relayed to the crawlers. The Operatic Collective, the Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and one more house all abdicate their spots on the ninth floor and announce they are leaving. The request is denied. While the Earth system is in quarantine, off-boarding is suspended under Syndicate rule 470.B through 495 of the System AI Stability Addendum. The teams remain as designated. The rules must be followed.

beats.headline: The Sultana behind her veils
beats.text: Arief calls the nagas a court of assassins, not warriors; no changeling or spy has ever reached their inner sanctum, and even Juice Box will not try. Their warlord is the Sultana, in life the crown princess and daughter of the naga king, play-acting the Sepsis Whore, the sultana of the old histories who had 198 daughters before 99 sons and supposedly poisoned almost all of the sons. In the old days, her honor guard were sentenced to deferred death for looking at her. The naga team loses every season. She has never once been killed in the game.

beats.headline: Always the first to fall
beats.text: The naga castle sits about eight miles from the border, on rocky ground chosen so nobody can tunnel in from below, and strangely close to Shanty Town. Historically it is almost always the first castle to fall. But every time, by the time the invaders reach the inner sanctum, the Sultana is gone. The team still loses its throne room. Its leader has never once been captured or assassinated since she took over, and she reappears at the end, laughing and joking. Nobody knows where she hides.

beats.headline: Four of eleven
beats.text: Eleven Naga entered Faction Wars this season. To free Donut and Katia from the Sepsis Whore business, four of them must die. Princess Vinata herself. Two assistants titled Ikbal, both her cousins, one of them married to Rishi. And the head of her castle guard, another cousin, rumoured to be her lover. The other seven are friends of the royal house or executives of the marketing agency that sells Naga tourism, and are not in the line of succession. Several of those seven, by the look of things, are already dead.

beats.headline: The first of the four
beats.text: Elle's team reaches the throne room. The guards there worship Emberus, just as Carl predicted, and they die, along with one big naga who worshipped no god at all. Katia gets the notification before anyone explains it: that was one of the four. The head of the castle guard. Carl adds that he was also the sultana's real-life boyfriend, and hopes she will be upset enough to make mistakes. Three left: Vinata and the two cousins. Then Edgar reports movement in the castle, non-corporeal, coming from below and moving up.

tagline.text: A hundred and fifty men with rifles, down to eighty and counting their bullets.
Arrived as a recap segment and left as a wipe.

beats.headline: Named on the recap
beats.text: The armed men from Africa get a name on the broadcast, and a graphic counting what is left of their ammunition.

beats.headline: Wiped
beats.text: Another recap carries the news: a city boss kills every one of them except a single man locked outside the boss room, and the remaining-crawler count drops below a million in the same broadcast.

tagline.text: What Donut's fans are calling themselves, according to Zev. The rival name, the Donut Holes, does not have her approval.
Fifty thousand retired crawlers who came back in, under the banner of a cat.

beats.headline: They are already there when he walks in
beats.text: Rosetta, Tipid, Justice Light and fifty thousand others have signed on. Carl gets emotional.

beats.headline: Digging in
beats.text: NPCs and former crawlers build the defences together: the changelings and the flesh golems started the stronghold, and a few thousand of the newcomers chose the Fortification Engineer race so they could build fast and level while they do it.

beats.headline: Congratulations, Champions
beats.text: Larracos and Shanty Town go to the twelfth floor under the Zerzura, and the two warlords of Team Retribution go with them. Ferdinand and Juice Box leave the realm, and under the current ruleset that is abandoning their posts. Team Retribution is defeated. The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars. The System addresses its congratulations to Champions.

tagline.text: Zebra-riding elves who favour poison, druid magic and long-range artillery. Outside the dungeon they are as humourless as the Skull Empire, and control half the universe's food.
Bald, pale elves with a territory of their own marked on the hunters' map of the grounds.
Half the food in the universe belongs to them, along with the entertainment channels, and they have a contract they intend to see honoured.
Their warlord is dead and their army is off the board.

beats.headline: A hunter of theirs, and the map on his body
beats.text: The group takes one of their hunters down and Carl loots him: an Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, and a crude map of the hunting grounds with a territory marked for every outfit working them. That is the first honest look anyone gets at how the hunt is organised. The Hive and the Skull Empire have both put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Dream have their own reasons for being here.

beats.headline: Elves at the door
beats.text: Two or three of the elves get a catapult set up and walk gas-rock artillery across the town. Carl uses Samantha to deliver missiles, delivers a villain's soliloquy while he is at it, and puts down another of their hunters.

beats.headline: Mister Gonorrhea Arrow
beats.text: On the broadcast, Carl puts the Dream among the no votes, its man too much of a walking abscess to change his mind despite sending members of his own family to die on this floor because someone said his mom is bangin'. Donut adds that she is quite attractive for a bald woman. On the walk to the stairs, Carl says he thinks the Dream will vote yes after all. They can change their votes right up until the start.

beats.headline: Threats over a lost vote
beats.text: The loss of the sponsors' protections does not go quietly. The Dream's cruiser threatens to nuke the planet over it, and is hobbled by a Syndicate Peacekeeper before it can. The Dream then threatens to stop food production unless the Epitome family is evacuated. They can scream and threaten all they want. Aboard a converted garbage freighter, the view is that once these AIs realise how much control they really have, the only thing stopping them is reason, and negotiation.

beats.headline: They buy a storyline instead of fighting for one
beats.text: Quasar has the warning ready before the sixty-hour ceasefire is out. The Dream have bought out the Vengeance of the Daughter and are pressing for fulfilment of the guaranteed third season written into it. An entertainment company, bought and aimed at a crawler.

beats.headline: They walk out of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan goes with them. What is left of the alliance is the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers, which is a smaller thing than it was that morning.

beats.headline: Epitome Tagg is dead, the Dream is finished
beats.text: Emberus wants Samantha interrogated and intends to break the floor in sixty-six minutes whatever the answer. In the middle of that, the Dream is beaten. Epitome Tagg is dead. Two teams remain standing on this floor, the Princess Posse and Team Retribution, and neither of them is the one that owned half the food in the universe.

tagline.text: Caprids. They own the tunnelling system, which is why anything that happens down here can be watched anywhere at all.
Carl's sponsor now. A full-grown goat stood in front of the cameras for fifteen seconds, bleated, and was gone.
Not a collective mind. A herd, and a herd bolts, which is why their matriarch treats a piece of news the way anyone else treats a loaded weapon.

beats.headline: The tunnelling system
beats.text: Mordecai catches the team up on the shape of the wider universe, and two powers come out of it: the Apothecary, and the Plenty. The Plenty built the tunnelling system a few hundred seasons ago and kept it proprietary. Before it, most of the universe got the crawl on a delay of anything from an hour to a year. Prosperity, in other words, is a thing they sell.

beats.headline: Judge us
beats.text: Three small jet-black goats with red eyes walk up to the art contest's judging table side by side, carrying no entry, with names like equations. Judge us, says the one in the middle. Carl gives them a five. They sigh as one, spin, and walk off: judgment received. Hurk the gleener shivers and says they are all like that, the adults worse, and nobody knows what goes on in their heads. The caprid on the crawl sits in a circle with them on a program every few days, screaming while they scream back.

beats.headline: The vacated sponsorship goes to them
beats.text: Carl signs autographs with the Popov brothers, poses for photographs with a fan who has a head tentacle named Maggie and strong views on the eradication of cocker spaniels, and finds out on the same afternoon who has bought him. The Plenty.

beats.headline: Two sponsors, one gift
beats.text: The Plenty and the Apothecary each send Carl and Donut something that protects them against vampirism, and they arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to compare notes. These two plainly do.

beats.headline: Carl works out who arranged it
beats.text: Kiwi and her dinosaurs arrive, Donut charms her with a potion, and somewhere in the middle of it Carl sees the shape of the thing: his own sponsor set the chain of events up, and wanted Miriam Dom to die at the end of it. A benefactor box is not a gift. It is a production note with a bow on it.

beats.headline: The herd finds out
beats.text: The goats start to panic and faint, certain the end times have come. Gamori, the matriarch, had known all of it and told none of them, because she knew precisely this would happen. Harbinger arrives to point out that he warned her, that he has been protecting the herd the whole time, and that they expelled him for it anyway.

beats.headline: The tunnels are not theirs
beats.text: The Plenty announce that they have lost control of the tunnel network outside the center system. Sydnee Iglacia, on air, calls it the first of the nine attacks: control. Gods from the dungeon keep appearing near the nodes, the checkpoints into the center system are overwhelmed, and the one place in the galaxy that still looks safe is the center. Prime Minister Victory is not so sure.

tagline.text: The system the Maestro and his brother are princes of. If the orcs' other system is a lemonade stand, Zev says, this one is Wal-Mart.
One of the oldest and largest of the system governments, orcish, rich on weapons, and famously bad at letting an insult go.
Its army is at the wall on the ninth floor and its king has come with it.
The books are not its own. A financial criminal lives inside the empire and pays handsomely for the address.

beats.headline: Carl plants a seed on Danger Zone
beats.text: A few minutes of provocation on a chat show, and the Skull Empire answers them with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht. It hits Manasa's trailer instead of Carl's, which was a mistake, and the Valtay answer that in turn by destroying the yacht, with his mother and the Maestro rumoured to be aboard. Three funerals come of it.

beats.headline: Algos, by celestial grenade
beats.text: The ball in Maggie My's hand is a celestial grenade: it summons the holder's god for sixty seconds and wraps the holder in Divine Intervention. Through Chris, relayed by Elle, comes where it came from. Maggie's sponsors are Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart, and so are Chris's. They sent her a scroll to choose a god, and Chris a box with a picture of Algos on it, so she knew which. Mordecai reads it as unofficial, a bribed one-on-one in a saferoom, and Algos as the god of pain: he would kill everyone in town in seconds.

beats.headline: A claim staked on the hunters' map
beats.text: The map off the dead hunter divides the hunting grounds between the outfits working them, and two of those outfits have put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Hive is one. The Skull Empire is the other.

beats.headline: Future Huntress
beats.text: Three of the Skull Empire's hunters try an ambush near an outcropping of the all-tree, which turns spells back on their casters. The Talent zaps himself dead with his own Lightning scroll, carrying almost 75,000 gold and a credit chit. The survivor is Future Huntress, level 50, a Boring Ol' Fighter who has not levelled once. She says top tens are fair game for anyone who bought the hunting license, that the empire paid for first crack at Carl, and that her death leaves him to the Dark Hive. Her highest stat is charisma.

beats.headline: The orcs vote yes
beats.text: Carl holds up a photo of the late Queen Consort Ugloo, mother of the Maestro and Prince Stalwart, killed when the Valtay blew up her yacht after the orcs accidentally killed a singer. The vote to turn off the sponsors' safety protocols stands at two to seven, and the two are Carl and Donut's new team and the Skull Empire. The orcs are crazy and they're all going to die, Carl tells the cameras, but they're not chickens.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: At an emergency session of the Syndicate Council, Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map, before the AI can infect the center system. She is in orbit herself, and says so. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she admits she would love them deposed, and insists that this is bigger. Prime Minister Glory counts the galaxy's wealth trapped in the system and the wars it would start. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. By 86%, she is muted.

beats.headline: King Rust at the wall
beats.text: The enemy's northern army masses at the edge of camp, and riding in at the head of the orcs, in full battle parade regalia, is the king himself. The Posse closes off the saferoom before anybody can drop a bomb through its door. Rust asks for an official parlay.

beats.headline: The parlay, and what his daughter told the Syndicate
beats.text: Rust explains it himself. Princess Formidable has commandeered one of his own warships and announced that she means to trip the Failsafe by hand. She has also told the Syndicate that the empire builds secret back doors into the security systems it sells. He asks Carl to send her a message on behalf of the people of Earth and trades a retreat for it. Rosetta takes his head off with a whip as he rides away, and the army charges.

beats.headline: Zev's aside, and Rosetta on Harry Tisch
beats.text: While the teams build their floats, Zev mentions in passing that Odette's husband has bought the rights to every show Donut has ever mentioned, and that it is probably all that is keeping the orcs solvent. Rosetta supplies the rest: his name is Harry Tisch, King Rust vetoed his extradition for tax fraud, and he has been working himself deeper into the empire ever since. Empires that sell weapons still have to bank somewhere.

beats.headline: Rent, tripled
beats.text: With D'Nadia dead, whoever is running the Skull Empire in the royal family's absence has swallowed every real estate holding of a group the Prism controlled. In the Makoka Cloud, Sydnee Iglacia's rent triples starting the next crutch, and oxygen is no longer included. She curses the Skull Empire, the Valtay and D'Nadia in the same breath.

tagline.text: A tax-exempt outfit nobody has heard of, which just won a sponsorship slot in a bidding war that ran to the final microsecond.
Crawlers who got out, and who want the whole thing stopped. Fifty thousand of them have come back in.
Every ship in orbit is theirs.

beats.headline: Carl's second sponsor
beats.text: Donut is taken by Veriluxx RealPet Companions and Katia by the Squim Conglomerate, and neither of those needs explaining: a pet brand wants the cat, a conglomerate wants the coverage. Carl is taken by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which is registered as a not-for-conquest, answers to no system government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.

beats.headline: One root vegetable
beats.text: The Valtay Corporation sends a neural enhancer, which is exactly the sort of thing a corporation sends. The Network sends a single Toraline root vegetable. Mordecai has never seen the plant, and can only guess at what it is for: a potion, an explosive, an inside joke. It is listed as very rare and worth about as much as an old shirt.

beats.headline: The emergency platinum box
beats.text: An Emergency Platinum Benefactor Box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network lands as a feral demon closes on the bowl. Mordecai reckons it cost more than the GDP of some star systems. Inside is one piece of glowing wicker: a head-throwing attachment made for Crawler Carl alone, inscribed with design approval from the Network's CEO. Carl's reading of it: a prize built for a coming floor, sent now because keeping him alive mattered more. He wonders aloud whether they sponsored a deity as well.

beats.headline: All in on him
beats.text: Behind the Network's money, a conversation. A woman asks how much they have spent, and Dr. Hu says it is best she does not know. They are going all in on Carl. She lists the risks: he is unstable, the Valtay are into everything, a civil war is coming. They should have sent instructions with the yam; half of it went on saving another crawler. He knows what it is really for, Hu says. Every time Carl goes on Odette's show, more people sign up. For his cause, she says. It is the same cause, Hu says. She calls him Porthus.

beats.headline: A potion and a note in code
beats.text: Signet warns that the dryads may call Diwata against the spreading brambles. Then a potion turns up in the benefactor box with a note that says only 'Save the toraline', until Carl's Escape Plan shows him the rest: Circe has sponsored Diwata, the potion is for Donut, and it is signed P. Hu. Whoever writes these has a view of the board that nobody standing on it has.

beats.headline: The first time a sponsor asks for something
beats.text: The request arrives through Zev, and it is a request rather than a present: go on Shadow Boxer. Carl agrees to it, reluctantly. Sponsors are supposed to send prizes and buy airtime. They are not supposed to want a favour.

beats.headline: A flyer for a shelter
beats.text: The Emergency Gold Benefactor Box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, the one a liaison tried to seize, holds a dirty, crumpled flyer and nothing else. The Shepherd's House in Homestead, Florida: don't spend Christmas alone, breakfast at 7 AM, all are welcome. Somebody has circled the 7 AM several times in red marker, and circled one more line among the rules. No pets allowed. Homestead is about forty minutes north of the Keys.

beats.headline: Why the authorities cracked down
beats.text: Tipid explains where the network came from. Doctor Hu formed it beside the Crawler Project: smaller, more focused, with far less support, and with the purpose of ending the crawl altogether. The residual in the homeless man's body at the Florida shelter, Paulie, was one of several actions that finally brought the authorities down on the non-profit.

beats.headline: Sponsoring Samantha's mother
beats.text: The Pacifist Network has sponsored the goddess Theia this season, on Carl's behalf, before anyone connected her to the Blood Sultanate. Theia is Samantha's mother. She was sponsored to help save Carl's life at the end of the fifth floor; in theory she is enraged at Samantha, but she has caused no trouble, appearing only to kill the demon Slit at the end of the bubble levels. It has closed a door on Vinata: Rosetta believes Theia is the goddess the sultana's court usually hides with. The sponsor is someone in the network's employ. Rosetta will not say who, only that it is not Porthus.

beats.headline: Stop the crawl, or else
beats.text: Timed for release just now, though shot a while ago under Rosetta's direction: Porthus behind a desk, announcing a new militant group that will move against every Syndicate governmental property and system in the known universe unless the crawl is stopped by the end of this one. Aboard Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in orbit, the enhancement zone weapons Porthus had installed are green across the board. Its pilot's card lists him as a captain in the Open Intellect Action Network. Boomer wants the lasers warmed up.

beats.headline: They take the orbit
beats.text: Lexis has the news and cannot get to the end of it. The Open Intellect Action Network has taken over every ship in orbit, and a third party she will not name has appeared at the kinder facility and is protecting it, confused. Then a message reaches her, and she stops talking, and she is afraid.

relations.note: Doctor Hu built the Crawler Project first; the Network is the half that wants the crawl stopped.

tagline.text: A democratic government of many races, whose army had a castle dropped on it before the season had properly started.
Caught cheating on the ninth floor, punished for it, and short one commander who took his own way out.

beats.headline: A castle lands on their army
beats.text: Quasar brings Carl the state of his ninth-floor team, and the state of it is that the castle came down in the middle of the Lemig Sortion's army. His people got clear and are building their own stronghold instead. The Lemig Sortion are the ones with a building in their camp.

beats.headline: Luke would like to leave
beats.text: Their man at the planning table is a small green goblin-looking alien called Luke, with the voice of a surfer. His people vote on everything, and undoing a vote takes eighty percent, which is why the Sortion is still in this war though its population sours on it every season. Juice Box points out that Carl's castle turned a bunch of his friends into zombies. When her demand goes into the queue, Luke says they're going to bail, if the people let them: there's seriously bad juju this season. He'll put a proposal to evacuate before the high congress. The Empress wishes him luck.

beats.headline: Commander Stockade goes to the sharks
beats.text: When the Desperado Club emptied, officials and players from several teams were thrown out into flooded Larracos, where the Semeru keep the concierge sharks fed and the castle submerged. Thirty-five were devoured, and only one was a warlord: Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion, a caterpillar-headed thing with several arms, the last of the thirty-five, torn apart on Odette's screen to laughter. He had not attended the meeting; a goblin-like proxy named Luke sat in for him.

beats.headline: Carl wakes up in their base
beats.text: Eleven hours gone, blood all over him, and most of the room around him killed by the thing riding inside him. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness had been arranging something together. It has come apart on top of them.

beats.headline: The field ruling
beats.text: Carl, Commander Stockade, Architect Houston and their adjutants convene for an official adjudication, and it goes on the record. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness used outside information to time a Summon Ally, meaning to pull Carl bodily to their base so that what was in him could be let loose on the rest of the Princess Posse. They got half of him, and the other half of the plan.

beats.headline: Punished, and the ceasefire ends early
beats.text: Panford, their adjutant, is left to explain the rampage through the base to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye, lost his mind, and finished it himself. Ferdinand gets an emergency action item passed for a live feed blackout so nobody can do this again. The Lemig Sortion is punished for cheating, the ceasefire ends early, and Carl goes home.

tagline.text: A megacorporation that is also a system government, living around its own star. An occasional entrant in this war, and a frequent winner of it.
Their pets arrive before they do: a swarm of Dumplins, every one of them carrying the Gurgles.
Several races who traded away everything but the brain for machinery, and kept going.
Warlord Fang hid inside his own pet, and the castle came down on the pair of them.

beats.headline: Rot stickers with the Gurgles
beats.text: The southern defence is already holding against the Dream, the Prism and the Nagas when the Reavers make their contribution: a horde of their own pet rot stickers, raised by hand to trust their masters, then juiced, infected and turned loose. This is a power that fights by handing you something diseased and standing back.

beats.headline: Through the bait-shop door
beats.text: The home anti-air battery goes up, then the hangar bay, and the flyers that buzzed Boomer turn into paratroopers coming down through the protections. Dozens of the Posse's names run down the casualty list. The worst of it is the saferoom: the bait shop sits inside the castle walls now, and Bomo notices a new door in the situational hallway belonging to the Reaver team. If any of the sponsors ever came in through that bait shop, the doggy door upgrade lets them come back the same way. It is the sneak attack Donut had just proposed, run backwards.

beats.headline: Carl gets the background on them
beats.text: Tina rampages, the compromised mages are put down, and somewhere in the middle of that Carl finally hears what a Reaver actually is. The real ones are all machine, with a little biological brain hidden somewhere inside the shell, and they can reshape themselves out of nanobot-sized parts. Anyone not vat-born who wants the citizenship gives up their biological form to get in the door and works off every upgrade after that.

beats.headline: What is left of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan and the Dream leave the alliance. That leaves the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers holding it, and the Reavers are not the sort of partner anyone chose.

beats.headline: The castle, the dragon and Fang
beats.text: The Reavers' robot dogs come at the rescue team inside the castle. Juice Box finds Louis, possesses him, teleports him out and leaves a heap of No Disassembles where he had been. Carl sets them off. The castle goes, the dragon goes, and Fang goes with it, hiding inside his own pet. Then Juice Box says the rest of it: they had been operating on Louis, and the heart and lungs he has now hold pieces of Epitome Tagg.

tagline.text: A name used as an insult: nobody in the Skull Clan wants to be mistaken for one.
Showrunners once. They ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and have not run a season since.
Cobra-headed, ruled out of the Blood Sultanate, and part of the push on the southern line.
The poverty was a performance. There were plans for the shipbuilding yards underneath it.
A signed offer on the table: citizenship for every native of Earth, in exchange for room in Earth's system.

beats.headline: The season that lost money
beats.text: By Odette's account, more than 250 cycles ago the Blood Sultanate of the Naga ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and they are still recovering. That season also handed out eighteen Celestial boxes, the most in any one season before this crawl, and was cursed for other reasons she declines to get into. The Nagas have not run a season since. They keep a standing place only because they bought a permanent spot early on.

beats.headline: In the southern push
beats.text: Carl and Donut join the defence in the south, and across the no-man's-land the Nagas hold the line beside the Dream and the Prism. Cobra-headed, and playing under the name of the Blood Sultanate, taken from a bloodier time in their own history.

beats.headline: The sultana at the table
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate's warlord materialises coiled next to Carl, half again the size of any naga he has seen: glossy white, a hint of gold along the hood, six arms in jingling golden bracelets, eyes solid red. Outside the dungeon she is the sultan's daughter, a war veteran and his lead advisor. In the game she portrays a historical queen of theirs called the Sepsis Whore. The Sultanate usually loses at once and plays to drive tourism, and it is still in after three other teams have fallen. Carl feels like a mouse in a snake's cage.

beats.headline: Prepotente takes their army apart
beats.text: Elle brings the count back. Most of the Naga army is already dead, and one goat did it, as payment for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Baroness Victory tells Carl he cannot work with him directly unless he signs on properly.

beats.headline: The airship at their castle
beats.text: Louis and Donut come at the Naga castle from the air. Elle and Imani go in on foot. Katia tells Carl that if this goes badly she wants him to have the flower, so that Donut at least reaches the next floor. Prepotente arrives to meet them.

beats.headline: Never broke at all
beats.text: Time freezes for the AI to announce the fight, and it uses the moment to tell everyone watching that outside the dungeon the Nagas had only been pretending to be poor. There were secret plans to seize the shipbuilding facilities. Then time restarts and the fight happens anyway.

beats.headline: Rishi's offer
beats.text: Their prisoner explains the Great Consensus, and that Vinata held to it, and that Vinata's group meant to steal the Naga fleet and leave the central system for good. Then he offers a signed document: citizenship in Naga lands for every native of Earth, if the Nagas may settle the other planets in Earth's system. Carl marks him with the ring and kills him.

beats.headline: Widow's Rights
beats.text: Outside the crawl, a bloody coup has put a new Sultan on the Naga throne, and his niece Chandra, one of Rishi's widows, has found a use for an old law: a royal widow may claim her husband's killer as her new husband. A public jury in Naga court found the idea of punishing Carl this way amusing and voted it through, adding the holdings of the defeated as his wedding gift in a fan box. As his wife she signs for him, she has filed to put Princess Donut's earnings under his conservatorship, and two Taurin associates have been paid to call on Quasar.

tagline.text: The ninth floor's own people, fielded as the defending team, and allied with the crawlers from the first hour of it.
Their warlord turned into an Unwashed on camera and told the audience that it is coming for them all.
One of two teams still standing at the end of the war.

beats.headline: The defending team names itself
beats.text: Carl and Donut come onto the ninth floor at Larracos, at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire, and the defending side already has a name it chose for itself. Cascadia runs through the rules. The crawlers ally with it against the Bloc, which is every other faction on the board.

beats.headline: Ferdinand holds the interface
beats.text: Juice Box and Louis are reunited, and he is visibly uneasy about the marriage. Then she lays out the practical problem: Ferdinand is mayor of Shanty Town, just outside Larracos, and he holds the warlord interface for the team, because he is technically from outside. Nothing this side of the wall moves without a cat's cooperation. Drick is the adjutant.

beats.headline: A blackout for everyone
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand proposes an emergency action item, in language unsuitable for the broadcast, because teams on other floors are cheating: nobody in the dungeon, including the guests partying in the centipede on the eighteenth floor, may watch any outside feed for the rest of the game. It is approved. Effective immediately, everyone in the dungeon is under a live-feed blackout. Carl had not wanted to spend one of his own action items on it. Victory notes that it is a first.

beats.headline: The acid trench
beats.text: Team Retribution's part in the assault is two spies and some scrolls. The NPCs were handed scrolls that change the chemistry of water in a container, instead of alcohol for some of their bars. So the spies drop a water scroll into the enemy's empty middle trench, turn it to acid, and cover the whole thing with an illusion. The enemy, confused and scared, fall back from the first trench and jump into it blind. The scout, an NPC porsuk bartender, goes up almost twenty levels.

beats.headline: The dwarves under the field
beats.text: A mage's dispel clears the Posse's smoke, and the ground under Carl, Donut, Rosetta, Simoom and the dead king's yak gives way. They land a dozen feet down among white dots outlined in green: Team Retribution's Semuru dwarves, two dozen of them, in a fortified tunnel big enough for cars. Juice Box had said passages like this cross the whole floor for the dwarven diggers. The dwarves re-form the roof and go after the war mages who fell in further down the line. Not so tough with the magic turned off.

beats.headline: It is coming for you all
beats.text: Odette arrives to replace Chaco, Cascadia comes apart on air, and Carl spends an emergency action item to shut the communication loophole the other teams have been using. Then Juice Box turns into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and tells everyone watching that it is coming for them all.

beats.headline: Two teams left
beats.text: Epitome Tagg is dead and the Dream is beaten, which leaves the Princess Posse and Team Retribution on the board. A team of NPCs was put on this floor to be fodder. It has outlasted eight galactic powers.

tagline.text: A collective mind spreading through the universe, and the thing the dungeon keeps drawing as the Krakaren.
Carl and Donut's third and final sponsor. Nobody on their side of it knows what she looks like.
One Primal who refused the collective, took the nine-tier attack, and is the reason anything biological is still here to watch this.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from her ability to synthesise elements, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: The third and final sponsor
beats.text: Clint has the account of Scolopendra's attack, and says the high elves were protected by something they had stolen. On the way back to Point Mongo the last sponsorship slot fills. The Apothecary takes it.

beats.headline: Their spokeswoman takes the floor
beats.text: A woman in a brown cloak patterned with circles and lines tells the stagehand not to cut Carl off, and he freezes. The people nearest her get up and move away. She cannot address Carl directly, she says, because she is one of his sponsors and it would breach the contract; she is also a sponsor of CrawlCon, and she has told them to let him speak. Then she walks out, and Circe Took calls her a bitch. Uptown Hal names her afterwards: the collective's spokeswoman.

beats.headline: The same gift, the same day
beats.text: She and the Plenty each send protection against vampirism, and the two parcels arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to coordinate. Carl now has two who do.

beats.headline: Their boxes are for the cat
beats.text: Minutes after Prepotente delivers a potion his sponsor meant for Princess Donut, Elle announces a benefactor box from the Apothecary, and Imani messages that she has one as well. Imani has opened hers. It is also for Donut. Donut, meanwhile, decides out loud that Carl's nipple-ring bribe was a trick, and that he was directed to give her that earlier potion all along.

beats.headline: Five boxes, all for the cat
beats.text: Five items on the table, all Apothecary sponsor boxes, each sent to a different crawler with a note saying it belongs to Princess Donut: a wand recharge scroll, a tiara, sheet music, an Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward that Borant tried and failed to block with an appeal, and an enchanted metal stick, named for someone Mordecai cannot place, given to Dmitri Popov. The hammer does nothing magical; the stick is no wand, but used correctly it can do something truly magical. Each carries a small seven worked into it. The one Apothecary box not meant for Donut went to Katia: a beanie that sank into her.

beats.headline: A mantra with mistakes in it
beats.text: Agatha's feed carries the Apothecary's chatter as well as her own team's. Thousands of its agents are seeded across the planet, ordered to kill themselves if they miss the dungeon. This season they mean to contact crawlers directly, in the dungeon or on the floor with the memory ghosts, and for months they have made their agents recite a daily mantra full of known inaccuracies and half-truths. The errors are there to keep the crawler alive around the showrunners. What the mantra really does is secretly implant a hidden upgrade.

beats.headline: A second pillow
beats.text: A platinum benefactor box arrives for Donut from the Apothecary in the same sitting as the tiara, and it holds a second charging pillow, purple where the first is red. The same ten-hour drain, and the same ruin after one hour. The difference is at the end of the description: this one drains any magical item, but transfers only to an absorption crystal on a like item. A ring's buff goes to a ring; sent to the wrong kind of item, the buff is lost. With two pillows, the tiara fills twice as fast.

beats.headline: The AI asks which side to take
beats.text: It wants advice from Orren and from Carl, and teleports Donut in as well, and it asks in a laboured metaphor about relationships: a girlfriend who looks like Agatha, and an older woman who has been giving it pointers on getting stronger, both of whom want the same man in prison dead. Donut tells it to find out whether he is really good or really bad before doing anything, and even then to stay out of it unless it has no choice.

beats.headline: The whole of it, on stage
beats.text: The AI gives the account itself. The Primals were individuals once, and their society spread until the warring and the waste made them decide to end it and keep their minds in one collective instead. Those who refused fled. The Apothecary was born near the end, engineered to meld into the whole, and joined the resistance instead. The collective became a weapon aimed at every remaining scrap of biological life, and when it let off the nine-tier attack she stood in front of it, and what grew back afterwards grew back behind her.

tagline.text: Dungeon-born magic elementals who stopped taking orders, and took the Gate with them on the way out.
Holding the castle at Larracos, six hours from taking the floor, and conscripting gods to keep it.
They leave with exactly what they came for, and a warning about Agatha on the way out.

beats.headline: Stalwart explodes and the Gate goes with them
beats.text: Carl and Samantha come out of the Party Planner into Reaver territory. Stalwart teleports in beside Elle and the waiting portal with a squad of war mages, Akuma among them. Then the mages around him chant, and Stalwart explodes, and Akuma teleports out holding the Gate of the Feral Gods. The war mages conscripted under Stalwart are nobody's soldiers now. They are a faction, which the rules do not have a slot for.

beats.headline: Two co-warlords, and a god on a leash
beats.text: They hold the Larracos castle, and six hours of holding it would take the floor. Baroness Victory reads out two co-warlords, Akuma and Agatha, and Akuma is not pleased about it. The Gate goes onto the Midnight Market and comes back as potions, and the potions conscript Yarilo. Fopsy, adjutant for the Dream, has a theory: that Agatha now thinks the AI is a danger to the Eulogist and wants the ascendency game over so it can be shut down.

beats.headline: Agatha walks off her post
beats.text: The system deems Warlord Agatha to have abandoned her post, and nobody, the adjutants included, can say why. She is removed, and Akuma is named sole warlord of the rebellion.

beats.headline: They quit the floor
beats.text: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat that the war mages are done here. They never wanted the castle; they came to test the potions and to find the Scavenger's Daughter, who was hidden inside it, and she is with them now. First, though, he wants Carl and Donut to kill Agatha, who was forced on the rebellion to get it system access: she is an enemy to them all. Then he leaves the realm, and under this season's rules the rebellion is recorded as defeated.

beats.headline: Five left, and a home overrun
beats.text: The war mages had lived in the Pineapple Cabaret. They left deliberately, back to cold storage, to be brought into Faction Wars and find the Scavenger's Daughter, and in the few days they were gone their protection spells failed and it was overrun: shadow mimics, the Ogre Imperium's leftovers, and older things Agatha could wake. There are five of them left. Plan one was more mages, plan two an old ally in the Nothing. Carl is plan three.

tagline.text: The affiliation on a flying mantis hunter's tag, level 61, blood tracker: the Dark Hive.
A mantis hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and Carl is on its list.

beats.headline: The Hive is hunting you
beats.text: A hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and the message it sends Carl is a note knifed to the saferoom door and signed by Vrah: the Hive is hunting him, there will be nowhere to hide, and his death will not be quick.

beats.headline: Circe Took's daughters
beats.text: The Dark Hive's party in the Hunting Grounds is a family concern. A CrawlCon audience that knows it well counts eight mantids left on the floor: seven warriors, all daughters of Circe Took, Vrah among them, and one male who stays in Zockau trading with the other representatives. Circe chairs Carl's panel herself, carves a chunk out of the table beside him, and on her way out promises to hunt down whoever harms her other daughters. Carl calls after her that it will be him.

beats.headline: Seven warriors down to one
beats.text: Carl kicks a wheeled bomb the system has named Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home out of the saferoom door and slams it. It kills the three remaining mantises, explosive protection and all. With the berserker and the sisters who went down with her, the seven warrior daughters are now one: Vrah, infected and airborne. The only other mantis on the floor is the male merchant holed up in Zockau, and Carl is already writing him a note offering protection in exchange for the gear.

beats.headline: A corporation that sells upward
beats.text: Edict explains the arrangement. The Dark Hive is a private corporation, and it sells everything it loots to the Burrowers, the royal family and government of the mantis system, who have paid in advance and expect delivery on the ninth floor. Edict's own family is of Deep Mind and employed by that government. Every mantis coupling must be registered ahead of time, with a trial and counseling for the male, and a government family may not couple with a for-profit one without a bond and a license.

tagline.text: A maker's name on a relay, a personal shield and a pulse pistol found in Agatha's shopping cart. None of it belongs down here.
A power outside Borant that answers an insult by taking a prince’s yacht apart with his family aboard, and does not explain itself afterwards.
A business that is also a nation, run by a parasite that pilots other people’s bodies, and it holds the paper on Borant’s debt.

beats.headline: A singer with a worm in her head
beats.text: Manasa, the cobra-headed pop star with the eighth-ranked single in the universe, died long ago; she contracted with the Valtay so that one of their parasites could keep her career going, and it is hotter than ever. On the panel she backs the Valtay's attempt to collect their debt from Borant. Then a pulse meant for Carl and Donut hits the trailer she swapped into, and she is gone. Their entertainment assets bring in more than their technology, Ripper says. Then the Valtay claim a dreadnought has destroyed Prince Stalwart's yacht.

beats.headline: A sponsor Borant cannot refuse
beats.text: The Admin notice arrives while Carl is still picking himself up beside the track: he has been sponsored, and viewers of his feed will now see his sponsor's advertisements. The sponsor is the Valtay Corporation. He answers Donut's question out loud with the name, then switches to chat: not a word about them out loud. Borant hates them; they are the ones trying to invade the Borant system, and they are the reason the show started when it did. Borant probably had no choice. It could mean good loot. It could mean Borant tries harder to get him killed.

beats.headline: Not shapeshifters at all
beats.text: Carl asks about the Valtay while Mordecai is explaining the local shapeshifters, and the answer is that they are not shapeshifters. They are a kind of creature called a Gondii. A Gondii enters a dead body within hours of death and reactivates it, reads its old memories, and can keep it running for centuries. Intellect Hunters do something similar, but their bodies begin to rot almost at once, so they are forever hopping. There is also something called an Infiltrator, which Mordecai calls much more insidious, and does not explain.

beats.headline: A creditor with a seat at the table
beats.text: A corporate system government inside the Syndicate, which is to say a company that is also a country and answers to neither description when it is inconvenient. Its people are parasites in the literal sense, riding the bodies of other races. It holds the Borant Corporation’s debt, and it sends a crawler a neural enhancer, which is the sort of gift that is also a note.

beats.headline: The liaison under the hood
beats.text: Orren, the Syndicate liaison who questions Carl over Loita's death, lets slip that the kua-tin intervened on the crawler's behalf and overruled his recommendation to remove him, and that the mudskippers are not known for recognising threats. If the rumors are correct and his own people take over after the next floor, he hopes they will listen to him. Then his hood slips. The swirling darkness is a face-shaped bowl of liquid, and in it Carl glimpses a worm. A Valtay worm.

beats.headline: An attorney for Borant
beats.text: A last-minute lawsuit tries to stop Carl's portal to the ninth floor, and its sole plaintiff is the Skull Empire. The Valtay, currently at odds with Borant, send an attorney to help Borant anyway, with an argument about Carl himself: he now owns stock in a company based in the Skull Empire, and a taxpayer not in arrears is treated differently, so the case belonged in a different court. It is dismissed. Neither the Valtay nor Borant is fond of the orcs.

beats.headline: Regency to the worms
beats.text: Two messages land the moment the interview ends. The first: a regency change has created a conflict of interest, so the Valtay Corporation is removed as one of Carl's sponsors, effective immediately, and an auction will fill the slot. The second goes to the whole planet. A Syndicate court has declared the Borant Corporation independent of the Borant System Government, which automatically executes an earlier ruling handing the Valtay 51% of the corporation. Borant still runs the crawl, and contracts stand, indentures included. Odette thanks the gods, then tells Carl: too bad it's the Valtay.

beats.headline: Borant's newest partners
beats.text: Seventy hours before the Masquerade, the daily announcement thanks Borant's newest partners, the Valtay Corporation, for the capital and help that let the next floor be finished just in time. That floor was not supposed to exist yet: what was going to be the seventh is now the eighth, with its difficulty raised to match. The Valtay have bought themselves a floor, and the crawlers are advised to stay as long as they can rather than go down early.

beats.headline: The floor that broke
beats.text: Mordecai has the story of the broken seventh floor from Mistress Tiatha, and he puts it on the engineers: they built the level just like the fairytale, and the goat did what the kid in the story took thousands of years to figure out. The Valtay are likely irritated with the Borant designers. The Apothecary and the Plenty probably did well out of providing the means, at the cost of the Valtay and the Syndicate, because the Syndicate pays in advance for the tunnels that carry the livestream, and a skipped floor is not refunded.

beats.headline: The Valtay solution
beats.text: The Valtay representative, a worm in the body that once belonged to the Syndicate Prime Minister's mother, assures the council all is perfectly normal. The solution the council backs is theirs: an extinction event, as fast as possible, because the quarantine lifts when the last crawler dies. Their mercenary guilds are recalled off Earth's surface, and the AI has agreed to let tens of thousands of fully armed mercenaries and the sponsors' private armies into the coming war, spread equally among the eight sponsored teams. Well over 150,000. The goal is every crawler, Carl and the cat first.

beats.headline: How a gondii takes a body
beats.text: Tipid, hit in the shoulder and talking too fast, explains what is inside the mages. A gondii worm can move into any dead form and take it over, memories included, though it takes time to learn what to look for and leaves big gaps at first. The Valtay charter says only the willing, and not every gondii lives on the right side of that law. Tipid has heard rumours of outlaw crews, and in a popular tunnel drama about one they are some of the most expensive mercs in the galaxy, at least on the show. A worm that does not care about its host can hop bodies and overclock them. Tipid rates them above the scree.

beats.headline: The Emperator's bomb
beats.text: The Emperator of the Valtay fleet comes through the tunnel gate carrying a system-busting bomb, apparently waiting for the AI to be distracted. It was not distracted. It says so in the middle of a floor announcement, read aloud by a mudskipper who had no idea the text was coming, and adds that it makes no apologies about where that giant suicide bomb just ended up. It does not say where. A creditor who arrives with a bomb has stopped negotiating.

beats.headline: A royalty clause, and a worm
beats.text: Sydnee Iglacia's publisher is a subsidiary of a Valtay company, and her contract lets them hold her royalties for the whole of her natural life, payable to heirs only on proof of her good moral character. The payments can be accelerated, if she signs a Valtay life contract and lets a worm take her over after death. It is not something she would ever dream of doing. Until her rent tripled, anyway.

tagline.text: Carl's spiderweb tattoo grants access to it. Mordecai's word for it is a cult.
A cult you join by accident, the moment you accept a gift from something that would prefer to be worshipped.

beats.headline: Membership arrives with the tattoo
beats.text: The guild worships a demigod, and access is granted by a tattoo that anyone who uses one of its artefacts receives whether or not they went looking for a guild. Mordecai notes, in the tone of a man reading a pamphlet he did not ask for, that it also runs outreach centres.

beats.headline: A map of the secret passages
beats.text: Past the carved door there is only a dark room and a voice like a naga's. It asks Carl whether he wants a job helping the family, and whether he means to kill Katia for the prize. No to both. He wants a map of the Desperado Club's secret passageways. A swarm of spiders runs up his arm, and his map fills: passages and tunnels, some with monsters in them, a hidden potion market on the middle floor, and a scattering of drug dens behind panels in the hallways.

beats.headline: She who brings the body
beats.text: The Night Wyrm's messages arrive as a job board would, in his hissing voice. The mark is dead, little sweets; bring her filthy body to the guild, because she who brings the body is she who gets paid. Katia brings it. Job Complete. And then the next line, in the same breath: I have more work for you. Yes, yes, there is always more. Come to me, and we will spread our family's power.

beats.headline: Hamed takes the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive and in her chair, tells Carl and Donut they are banned from the Desperado Club by the new management, who has banned all crawlers for his first few days. He keeps bodyguards with him at all times, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers, and more security than she has ever seen. The surviving cretins and sai were airlocked off to the mercenary markets. His name is Hamed: the Night Wyrm, leader of the Guild of Suffering, husband of the late Astrid, and father of Damascus Steel and Anaconda, who are supposedly in the club hunting him.

relations.note: Use the artefact, take the tattoo, and you are a member.

entities.name: The Nebular Sin Patrol
entities.role: Hunting team of a nomadic cult

tagline.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol. A name on a dead hunter's map: one of the groups given ground near Zockau, with Prepotente and Miriam Dom claimed as targets.
The Nebular Sin Patrol: trainee priests of a nomadic, self-augmenting cult who consider anyone born on a seeded world an abomination, and hunt crawlers as a crusade.
The Nebulars. They worship the AI at the centre of the galaxy, call imitations blasphemy, and want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one. They sponsor Sister Ines.

beats.headline: Circled on a dead man's map
beats.text: A map off a dead hunter. The hunters sat down and divided the floor between them: the Hive has the bottom left, the Dream holds Point Mongo, and the unaffiliated are relegated to the country around Zockau, among them groups called the Crafters and the Nebular Sin Patrol. Some groups have also claimed specific crawlers. The Nebular group's names are Prepotente and Miriam Dom. It is a hunting licence, drawn in pencil, and it ended up in the wrong hands.

beats.headline: Sand people in bishop hats
beats.text: The CrawlCon audience briefs Crawler Carl. The Nebulars are camping out and claiming the right to hunt him too, since he is in their territory, and they are pushing back against the Dark Hive: the nebs and the mantids fought a war once. They are not a race but a religious cult that augments itself as a sacrament. They settle hard planets, engineer their children to survive them, then half move on. Soothers, humans, elves and more, all in the same full-body outfit. Carl pictures sand people in bishop hats.

beats.headline: Priests in training
beats.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol attends nearly every crawl with different hunters each time: young males, studying for the priesthood, trained for the event. Anyone born on a seeded planet is an abomination to them, and hunting one is a crusade. They spend heavily, sometimes on a deity sponsorship, and campaign for the right to run a crawl of their own. They favour cleric and paladin targets, hence Prepotente and Miriam Dom. Someone mentions they botched an attack on Lucia Mar a few days ago.

beats.headline: Caught between mantises and a hob-lobber
beats.text: Zockau. A group of robed priests opens up on Crawler Carl's doorway with magic missiles and fireballs and hits a mantis warrior too. Her sisters take it personally. Carl drops a hob-lobber into the argument and kills three priests; the mantises are protected against explosives. A berserking mantis tears into what remains, and Carl marks three more with his Ring of Divine Suffering before she cuts them down. The first is a young human under the robe, name starting with Q. By the end, every neb is dead.

beats.headline: A stadium full of hats
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut plays an arena card and gets a colosseum with adjustable gravity and landscaping and a capacity crowd: thousands upon thousands of robe-clad people in large hats. Crawler Carl recognises them from the hunters on the last floor. The Nebulars, the nomadic religious cult. The card does not let Donut change the audience, only how much it likes them, and she has set that to the top. It cheers every time she adjusts the grass. Mongo screeches.

beats.headline: Cousins of the Reavers
beats.text: Faction wars briefing, on the Reavers: a megacorporation and system government living on a Dyson sphere, who were supposedly once related to the Nebulars, the religious nuts who sent a team called the Nebular Sin Patrol to die as hunters on the sixth floor. Like the nebs, the Reavers began as several biological races who enhanced themselves with machines. The Reavers kept going, until only the brains were left. The Nebulars stopped somewhere short of that.

beats.headline: Sister Ines's patron
beats.text: Recap commentary on the zombie event. It had started to disrupt Sister Ines's charm poem, but her sponsor and patron, the Nebulars, had helped her raise the Word Weaver spell to level fifteen, so she controlled the boss, the spells the boss could cast, and therefore the zombies. The charm is strong enough that fish haul themselves out of the ocean to get closer. The commentator's co-host notes that Princess Donut could only dream of charm like that.

beats.headline: What the Nebs want
beats.text: Mordecai remembers: the Nebular team has been sponsoring Ysalte, as well as Sister Ines. What they want is simple. An ancient, stable AI near the galaxy's centre runs a benign enhancement zone over several systems, and the Nebs worship it and call its imitations blasphemy. They hunt, they play the Celestial Ascendency for a seat on the crawl council, and they want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one, every person on it, and every other religion. Crawler Carl notes this is not pacifism.

beats.headline: Pontifex Shine's goddess
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte, level two hundred and fifty, arrives with her paperwork attached: this goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. The sponsor is not currently inside the shell, so she speaks and acts according to her regular nature, which, the warning adds, is bad news. The Nebulars have paid for a god and are not driving it.

beats.headline: A crackpot theory's origin
beats.text: An orc warlord explains why his daughter is determined to destroy the system: she believes the local AI's insanity is contagious, and that it could reach the centre system and collapse their way of life. He grunts that there is no proof anything like that can happen. It would be like a gnat taking down one of his corvettes. It is a crackpot theory, and it originated, he says, with those Nebular idiots. The analysts dismiss it. His daughter is convinced.

beats.headline: A colony, gone
beats.text: The galactic news after the war, as York watches it. A new prime minister. A Dream cruiser crashed onto the surface of Earth over Australia. The mass suicide of one of the Nebular colonies. But mostly, the talk is of the Mantis system, which has simply gone boom.
